Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):

[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. - structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).

Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).

- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,

- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

output.page_summary: Connective tissues are compared by location and function: loose, dense, elastic, specialised tissues (cartilage, bone and blood), and adipose. The plant diagram divides tissues into meristematic and permanent, traces their subtypes, and locates apical, intercalary and lateral meristems.

items.content: Types of Connective Tissues. Columns: Type of Tissue | Location | Function. Rows: Loose connective tissue; Dense connective tissue; Elastic connective tissue; Specialised connective tissue—(i) Cartilage, (ii) Bone, (iii) Vascular connective tissue (blood); Adipose tissue.

items.content: Type of Tissue: Loose connective tissue | Location: Deep layers of skin, blood vessels, nerves and body organs. | Function: Support and elasticity.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How does loose connective tissue compare with dense connective tissue in this table?
teacher_understanding.answer: Loose tissue is associated with deep skin layers, blood vessels, nerves and organs, providing support and elasticity; dense tissue is associated with tendons and ligaments and provides great strength.

teacher_understanding.question: Does 'loose' mean that the tissue gives no support?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Its fibres are relatively loosely arranged, allowing packing and flexibility rather than the tightly bundled resistance typical of dense tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful around vessels, nerves and organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: These structures need to remain supported while nearby parts move; a flexible connecting material accommodates movement without making the region rigid.

prerequisites: Tissue as a group of cells and surrounding material
items.exam_note: Distinguish flexible packing around structures from dense tissue in tendons and ligaments.

why_chain.step: Organs, vessels and nerves need support without being fixed rigidly.
Loose connective tissue provides support and elasticity in these regions.

unpack.example_or_place: Think beneath the skin and around the vessels and nerves passing through it.
unpack.consequence: Support need not mean hard or immovable tissue.
unpack.visual_verb: Cushion a vessel with an open fibre mesh.
unpack.level_extra: Use location and function together in matching questions.

items.content: Type of Tissue: Dense connective tissue | Location: Tendons and ligaments | Function: Compactly pack structures to one another and provides great strength.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: What contrast does the table make between dense and loose connective tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Dense tissue forms strong connections in tendons and ligaments, whereas loose tissue supports structures such as vessels, nerves and organs with elasticity.

teacher_understanding.question: How do tendons and ligaments differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Tendons connect muscle to bone; ligaments connect bone to bone at joints.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do these connections need dense tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Pulling muscles and moving joints place tension on their connections. Closely packed collagen fibres help resist that pulling force.

items.exam_note: Tendon versus ligament is a useful related distinction; both belong to dense connective tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: पास-पास भरे मज़बूत रेशों वाला जोड़ने का tissue
terms.everyday_image: कई धागे मिलकर मज़बूत रस्सी बनाते हैं

terms.plain_meaning: tendon muscle को bone से, ligament bone को bone से जोड़ता है
terms.everyday_image: हड्डियों के पास खिंचाव सहने वाली मज़बूत पट्टियाँ

why_chain.step: Muscle pull and joint movement can strain connections.
Dense connective tissue supplies strong, compact connections in tendons and ligaments.

unpack.example_or_place: The Achilles tendon behind the ankle is a familiar tendon example.
unpack.consequence: Dense means strong fibrous connection, not mineralised hardness like bone.
unpack.visual_verb: Bundle fibres and pull on the bundle.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid reversing muscle–bone and bone–bone connections.

items.content: Type of Tissue: Elastic connective tissue | Location: Lungs, arteries, trachea and vocal cords. | Function: Provides elasticity.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How do the listed roles of elastic and dense connective tissues compare?
teacher_understanding.answer: Elastic tissue provides elasticity in lungs, arteries, trachea and vocal cords; dense tissue provides great strength in tendons and ligaments.

teacher_understanding.question: How does elasticity differ from simply being strong?
teacher_understanding.answer: Elasticity means recovering shape after deformation. Strength concerns resisting damage or breaking under force; the two properties are not identical.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is recoil useful in lungs and arteries?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lungs expand during breathing and arteries stretch as blood is pumped into them. Elastic fibres help these structures return toward their previous dimensions.

prerequisites: Arteries carry blood from the heart
items.exam_note: Remember the full location set, including trachea and vocal cords.

terms.plain_meaning: खिंचकर फिर पुराने आकार की ओर लौटने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: खींचा हुआ रबर छोड़ते ही लौटता है

terms.plain_meaning: गले में आवाज़ बनाने के लिए कंपन करने वाली तहें
terms.everyday_image: बोलते समय गले के अंदर कंपन

why_chain.step: Breathing and blood pulses repeatedly stretch body structures.
Elastic connective tissue supplies elasticity in the listed structures.

unpack.example_or_place: Follow an inhalation into the lungs and a heartbeat into an artery.
unpack.consequence: Stretch and recoil should be distinguished from rigid support.
unpack.visual_verb: Stretch and recoil.
unpack.level_extra: A location may contain several tissues; tracheal cartilage and elastic tissue are not contradictory.

items.where_on_page: specialised connective tissue group, first subrow
items.content: Type of Tissue: Specialised connective tissue—(i) Cartilage | Location: Ends of long bones, tip of nose, parts of larynx and trachea. | Function: Provides flexibility and support.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How are cartilage and bone compared on the page?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cartilage provides flexibility and support at long-bone ends, the nose tip and parts of the larynx and trachea. Bone provides protection, support and muscle attachment.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cartilage not simply another name for bone?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cartilage has a firm but relatively flexible matrix, whereas bone has a mineralised matrix giving much greater rigidity.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is cartilage useful at bone ends and in the airway?
teacher_understanding.answer: At joint surfaces it helps provide smooth, cushioning contact. In parts of the airway it supports the passage while allowing some flexibility.

prerequisites: Matrix as material around tissue cells
items.exam_note: Match cartilage with flexible support; do not assign bone-like rigidity to it.

terms.plain_meaning: सहारा देने वाला, bone से ज़्यादा लचीला tissue
terms.everyday_image: नाक का सिरा हल्के दबाव पर थोड़ा मुड़ जाता है

terms.plain_meaning: आवाज़ बनने वाला हिस्सा और उससे नीचे हवा जाने की नली
terms.everyday_image: गले से छाती तक जाती साँस की राह

why_chain.step: Some body parts need shape and support without becoming completely rigid.
Cartilage supplies flexibility and support at the listed sites.

unpack.example_or_place: Nose tip; ends of long bones near a joint.
unpack.consequence: Specialised connective tissues include both flexible cartilage and rigid bone.
unpack.visual_verb: Bend the nose tip and cushion bone ends.
unpack.level_extra: The page says parts of the larynx and trachea, not that these organs consist entirely of cartilage.

items.where_on_page: specialised connective tissue group, second subrow
items.content: Type of Tissue: Specialised connective tissue—(ii) Bone | Location: Bones | Function: Protection and support muscle attachment.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: Which functions distinguish the bone row from the blood row?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone provides protection, support and muscle attachment; blood transports oxygen and carbon dioxide and contributes to immune response and clotting.

teacher_understanding.question: How does bone support differ from cartilage support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Bone's mineralised matrix makes it rigid enough for load-bearing and protective frameworks; cartilage provides relatively flexible support.

teacher_understanding.question: How does muscle attachment to bone help movement?
teacher_understanding.answer: A contracting muscle transmits force through its tendon to a bone, moving that bone about a joint.

items.exam_note: Read the compressed function cell as protection, support and muscle attachment.

terms.plain_meaning: वह जुड़ाव जिससे muscle का खिंचाव bone तक पहुँचता है
terms.everyday_image: डोरी खींचने पर उससे जुड़ा डंडा घूमता है

why_chain.step: The body needs a framework that bears loads and receives muscle pull.
Bone supplies support, protection and attachment for muscles.

unpack.example_or_place: The skull protects the brain; limb bones act as levers.
unpack.consequence: Bone is living connective tissue, not merely a passive hard object.
unpack.visual_verb: Shield an organ and pull a bone lever.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish tissue name 'bone' from the whole organ, which also contains other tissues.

items.where_on_page: specialised connective tissue group, third subrow
items.content: Type of Tissue: Specialised connective tissue—(iii) Vascular connective tissue (blood) | Location: Within blood vessels | Function: Transport of oxygen and carbon dioxide and immune response blood clotting.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How does blood's role differ from the supporting tissues in this table?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blood works within blood vessels in gas transport, immune response and clotting, rather than chiefly providing the mechanical support listed for cartilage and bone.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can fluid blood belong to connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connective tissue need not be solid. Blood has cells suspended in a fluid extracellular matrix, plasma, and links body regions by transport.

teacher_understanding.question: How can blood perform transport, defence and clotting?
teacher_understanding.answer: Red blood cells carry most oxygen, white blood cells participate in defence, and platelets with clotting factors help form clots. Carbon dioxide is transported in several forms, much of it as bicarbonate.

prerequisites: Oxygen use and carbon dioxide production
items.exam_note: Blood is a specialised connective tissue; do not confuse animal 'vascular' tissue with plant xylem and phloem.

terms.plain_meaning: blood vessels में बहने वाला, चीज़ें एक जगह से दूसरी जगह पहुँचाने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: सड़कों पर सामान पहुँचाती गाड़ियाँ

terms.plain_meaning: कीटाणों या दूसरी हानिकारक चीज़ों के खिलाफ शरीर की प्रतिक्रिया
terms.everyday_image: घाव में आए कीटाणों से शरीर की लड़ाई

terms.plain_meaning: चोट पर blood का थक्का बनकर बहाव रोकने में मदद करना
terms.everyday_image: छोटी कटने की जगह पर जमा थक्का

why_chain.step: Distant cells need gas delivery and waste removal, while injuries need defence and sealing.
Blood performs gas transport, immune response and clotting.

unpack.example_or_place: Blood flowing from the lungs to body tissues; a clot after a small cut.
unpack.consequence: Connective tissue classification includes fluid as well as solid tissues.
unpack.visual_verb: Carry gases, intercept germs and seal a cut.
unpack.level_extra: Keep the three listed functions separate in statement-combination questions.

items.content: Type of Tissue: Adipose tissue | Location: Deep layers of skin, surrounding heart and kidneys and padding around joints. | Function: Support, protection, heat conservation and energy source.
items.type_note: A location–function comparison row, not merely a figure.

teacher_understanding.question: How does the adipose row compare with loose connective tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both occur in deep skin layers and provide support. Adipose is additionally listed around the heart, kidneys and joints, with protection, heat conservation and an energy role.

teacher_understanding.question: How do energy storage and heat conservation differ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Stored fat can be used as fuel; insulation slows heat loss. These are distinct functions of the same tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is adipose useful beneath skin and around organs?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its fat-rich cells form soft padding that cushions structures, and a subcutaneous layer reduces heat loss while retaining a reserve of chemical energy.

items.exam_note: Adipose is not just an energy store: protection, support and heat conservation are also listed.

terms.plain_meaning: fat जमा करने वाला tissue, जो नरम padding भी बनाता है
terms.everyday_image: नरम कुशन के साथ रखा हुआ ईंधन

terms.plain_meaning: शरीर की गर्मी जल्दी बाहर न जाने देना
terms.everyday_image: कंबल गर्मी बनने के बजाय गर्मी का निकलना कम करता है

why_chain.step: Organs need cushioning and the body needs to limit heat loss and retain fuel.
Adipose provides protection, support, heat conservation and an energy source.

unpack.example_or_place: Under the skin, around the heart and kidneys, and padding around joints.
unpack.consequence: A single connective tissue can serve mechanical, thermal and energy functions.
unpack.visual_verb: Pad an organ, slow escaping heat and store fat.
unpack.level_extra: Do not reduce adipose function to obesity or energy storage alone.

items.content: Plant Tissues → Meristematic tissue and Permanent tissue. Meristematic tissue → Apical meristem, Intercalary meristem, Lateral meristem. Permanent tissue → Simple permanent tissue and Complex permanent tissue. Simple permanent tissue → Parenchyma, Collenchyma, Sclerenchyma. Parenchyma → Aerenchyma and Chlorenchyma. Sclerenchyma → Sclerenchyma fibers and Sclereids. Complex permanent tissue → Xylem and Phloem. Connecting lines indicate classification, not a time sequence.
items.type_note: Classification, rather than the proposed figure: each branch assigns tissue types to a parent group.
prerequisites: Parent and child groups in a classification tree
items.exam_note: Trace complete parent–child paths; neighbouring labels are not necessarily siblings.

items.content: Plant Tissues: root group branching to Meristematic tissue and Permanent tissue.
items.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two groups begin the plant classification?
teacher_understanding.answer: The root divides into meristematic tissue and permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the main distinction behind this division?
teacher_understanding.answer: Meristematic cells actively divide; permanent tissues are differentiated and generally no longer actively dividing.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does a plant need both groups?
teacher_understanding.answer: It needs cells that generate growth and differentiated tissues that perform tasks such as support, photosynthesis and transport.

items.exam_note: Recognise the first-level division before identifying lower branches.

terms.plain_meaning: पौधे में मिलकर काम करने वाले cells के समूह
terms.everyday_image: एक पौधे में बढ़ने की जगहें और काम सँभालने वाले हिस्से

why_chain.step: Plants need both continuing growth and specialised work.
The tree separates meristematic and permanent tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: A growing shoot contains both growth regions and mature tissue.
unpack.consequence: All later labels must be traced back to one of these two branches.
unpack.visual_verb: Split the root into two branches.
unpack.level_extra: Do not read classification arrows as transport arrows.

items.content: Meristematic tissue: child of Plant Tissues; parent of Apical meristem, Intercalary meristem and Lateral meristem.
items.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which meristems belong to this branch?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical, intercalary and lateral meristems are its three displayed children.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes these three kinds?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are distinguished by position: tips, regions between mature tissues, and sides of stems or roots.

teacher_understanding.question: How does meristematic tissue produce growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Repeated cell division generates new cells, which can enlarge and differentiate into tissues.

items.exam_note: These three names classify meristems by position.

terms.plain_meaning: जहाँ cells बार-बार बँटकर नए cells बनाते हैं
terms.everyday_image: पौधे की नई बढ़त बनाने वाली छोटी कार्यशाला

why_chain.step: A growing plant needs a continuing supply of new cells.
Meristematic tissue supplies them through division at growth regions.

unpack.example_or_place: Shoot tips, root tips and other growth regions.
unpack.consequence: Different growth locations produce different kinds of increase in size.
unpack.visual_verb: Divide cells at three positions.
unpack.level_extra: Separate positional classification from the permanent-tissue branches.

items.content: Apical meristem: child of Meristematic tissue.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which group contains apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It belongs to the meristematic branch, alongside intercalary and lateral meristems.

teacher_understanding.question: How does apical differ from lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Apical meristems occur at root and shoot tips and contribute to length growth; lateral meristems contribute mainly to increased thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is growth at a tip useful?
teacher_understanding.answer: New cells near the advancing tip allow roots and shoots to extend into new soil or above-ground space.

items.exam_note: Apical means tip; relate position to length growth.

terms.plain_meaning: जड़ या shoot के सिरे पर नए cells बनाने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: टहनी की बढ़ती नोक

why_chain.step: Roots and shoots need to extend into new space.
Cell production near their tips contributes to length growth.

unpack.example_or_place: A growing shoot tip; root tips are a related standard example.
unpack.consequence: Tip growth is distinct from thickening.
unpack.visual_verb: Extend the tip.
unpack.level_extra: Use apical–tip–length as a linked association.

items.content: Intercalary meristem: child of Meristematic tissue.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which branch contains intercalary meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is one of the three types under meristematic tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How is its position different from an apical meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It occurs between differentiated regions, commonly near leaf or internode bases in grasses, rather than at the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: How can this position help grass regrow after cutting?
teacher_understanding.answer: If a basal growth region remains intact, its dividing cells can continue producing growth even after upper portions are removed.

items.exam_note: Intercalary is not synonymous with lateral; grass regrowth is a useful application.

terms.plain_meaning: बड़े हो चुके हिस्सों के बीच बचा नए cells बनाने वाला क्षेत्र
terms.everyday_image: घास कटने के बाद नीचे बचे हिस्से से फिर बढ़ती है

why_chain.step: Growth can be needed away from the terminal tip.
Intercalary regions allow local elongation between mature tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Bases of leaves or internodes in grasses.
unpack.consequence: Removing an upper part need not remove every growth region.
unpack.visual_verb: Lengthen a segment from its base.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the absolute claim that all plants or all nodes have intercalary meristems.

items.content: Lateral meristem: child of Meristematic tissue.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which larger tissue group includes lateral meristem?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristem lies under meristematic tissue, not permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does lateral growth differ from apical growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lateral meristems add to girth, whereas apical meristems contribute primarily to length.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a meristem along a stem's sides increase thickness?
teacher_understanding.answer: Its divisions add cells in cylindrical layers, increasing the stem's diameter.

items.exam_note: Associate lateral meristem with girth; cambium is a standard example.

terms.plain_meaning: तने या जड़ की बगल की दिशा में cells जोड़कर मोटाई बढ़ाने वाला हिस्सा
terms.everyday_image: पेड़ का तना सालों में मोटा होता जाता है

why_chain.step: A growing woody plant needs greater supporting and conducting capacity.
Lateral meristems add tissue that increases girth.

unpack.example_or_place: Cambium in a thickening woody stem.
unpack.consequence: Length increase and thickness increase should not be interchanged.
unpack.visual_verb: Widen a stem cylinder.
unpack.level_extra: Not every plant exhibits the same pattern of secondary thickening.

items.content: Permanent tissue: child of Plant Tissues; parent of Simple permanent tissue and Complex permanent tissue.
items.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which two branches divide permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple permanent tissue and complex permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does permanent differ from meristematic tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Permanent tissue consists of differentiated cells specialised for particular work; meristematic tissue retains active cell division.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does growth need to be followed by differentiation?
teacher_understanding.answer: Merely adding cells does not create efficient transport, photosynthesis or support; cells must acquire suitable structures and functions.

items.exam_note: Permanent does not mean necessarily dead.

terms.plain_meaning: किसी खास काम के लिए रूप ले चुका tissue, जिसके cells आम तौर पर सक्रिय रूप से नहीं बँटते
terms.everyday_image: सीखने के बाद अलग-अलग काम सँभालते कर्मचारी

why_chain.step: A plant needs specialised work as well as new cells.
Differentiated tissues provide that work and are grouped here as permanent tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Leaf tissue and conducting tissue in a stem.
unpack.consequence: Both simple and complex tissues belong to the permanent branch.
unpack.visual_verb: Differentiate cells and branch into two groups.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid equating permanent with dead or biologically inactive.

items.content: Simple permanent tissue: child of Permanent tissue; parent of Parenchyma, Collenchyma and Sclerenchyma.
items.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which three groups are simple permanent tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma are the three displayed groups.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinguishes simple from complex permanent tissue?
teacher_understanding.answer: Simple tissue is composed mainly of one similar cell type, while complex tissue combines different cell types working together.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does 'simple' not mean unimportant?
teacher_understanding.answer: The name describes cell-type composition, not importance; simple tissues perform major functions such as storage, photosynthesis and support.

items.exam_note: Xylem and phloem are not children of this branch.

terms.plain_meaning: मुख्य रूप से एक जैसे प्रकार के cells से बना काम करने वाला tissue
terms.everyday_image: एक जैसे कामगारों की टोली

why_chain.step: Some tissue tasks can be handled by similar cells together.
Such cell-type composition distinguishes simple from complex tissue.

unpack.example_or_place: Soft parenchyma in potato is a familiar example.
unpack.consequence: The three child names should be learnt as one sibling set.
unpack.visual_verb: Branch to three tissue names.
unpack.level_extra: Simple/complex refers to composition, not easy/difficult work.

items.content: Complex permanent tissue: child of Permanent tissue; parent of Xylem and Phloem.
items.type_note: The label names a classification group.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissues belong to the complex permanent branch?
teacher_understanding.answer: The diagram places xylem and phloem here.

teacher_understanding.question: How is their composition different from simple tissues?
teacher_understanding.answer: Each combines multiple cell types that cooperate in transport and related support functions.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can transport tissue need several cell types?
teacher_understanding.answer: Conduction, support and maintenance impose different requirements, which different specialised cells can meet together.

items.exam_note: Both xylem and phloem are complex permanent tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: अलग-अलग प्रकार के cells मिलकर एक जुड़ा काम करते हैं
terms.everyday_image: डिलीवरी में ड्राइवर, पैकिंग करने वाला और मददगार साथ काम करते हैं

why_chain.step: Long-distance transport requires coordinated tasks.
Different cell types cooperate in complex tissues.

unpack.example_or_place: Conducting bundles in a stem.
unpack.consequence: A tissue may contain multiple cell types without being an organ.
unpack.visual_verb: Combine different cells into a conducting bundle.
unpack.level_extra: Do not classify tissues by the apparent complexity of their names.

items.content: Parenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue; parent of Aerenchyma and Chlorenchyma.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype and its children.

teacher_understanding.question: Which specialised forms branch from parenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Aerenchyma and chlorenchyma are shown beneath parenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does parenchyma differ from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Parenchyma usually has living, relatively thin-walled cells; mature sclerenchyma commonly has dead cells with thick, lignified walls.

teacher_understanding.question: How can parenchyma support several different roles?
teacher_understanding.answer: Living cells can store substances, develop chloroplasts for photosynthesis, or be arranged with large air spaces for aeration.

items.exam_note: Aerenchyma and chlorenchyma belong under parenchyma, not alongside it as independent top-level groups.

terms.plain_meaning: आम तौर पर पतली दीवार वाले जीवित cells का tissue, जो भराव और अलग-अलग काम कर सकता है
terms.everyday_image: आलू का नरम अंदरूनी हिस्सा

why_chain.step: Plants need living tissue for storage and other metabolic work.
Parenchyma can specialise further for air spaces or photosynthesis.

unpack.example_or_place: Potato storage tissue and green leaf tissue.
unpack.consequence: A broad tissue group may have functionally specialised forms.
unpack.visual_verb: Split parenchyma into air-space and green forms.
unpack.level_extra: Keep the hierarchy intact in odd-one-out questions.

items.content: Collenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which group contains collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is a simple permanent tissue, grouped with parenchyma and sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does collenchyma differ from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Collenchyma has living cells with uneven wall thickening and provides flexible support; sclerenchyma commonly has dead, heavily thickened cells providing firmer support.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is flexible support useful in young plant parts?
teacher_understanding.answer: Young stems and leaf stalks must resist bending forces while still allowing growth and movement.

items.exam_note: Flexible support is a useful distinguishing association.

terms.plain_meaning: जीवित cells वाला tissue, जो बढ़ते हिस्सों को लचीला सहारा देता है
terms.everyday_image: नरम टहनी मुड़ती है लेकिन तुरंत टूटती नहीं

why_chain.step: Young parts need support without rigidly blocking growth.
Unevenly thickened living cells provide flexible support.

unpack.example_or_place: Below the surface of many young dicot stems and in leaf stalks.
unpack.consequence: Support tissues need not all be dead or rigid.
unpack.visual_verb: Bend a supported young stem.
unpack.level_extra: Do not confuse collenchyma with chlorenchyma despite similar spelling.

items.content: Sclerenchyma: child of Simple permanent tissue; parent of Sclerenchyma fibers and Sclereids.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype and its children.

teacher_understanding.question: Which forms branch from sclerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma fibers and sclereids are its two displayed forms.

teacher_understanding.question: How does it differ from collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclerenchyma commonly has dead cells at maturity with thick lignified walls, whereas collenchyma has living cells with uneven thickening and greater flexibility.

teacher_understanding.question: Why do thick lignified walls suit support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Lignin strengthens and stiffens the walls, allowing them to resist deformation even after the cell contents are lost.

items.exam_note: Fibers and sclereids are forms of sclerenchyma, not complex tissues.

terms.plain_meaning: मोटी और कड़ी दीवारों वाला tissue, जो मज़बूती देता है
terms.everyday_image: नारियल के बाहरी रेशे और कठोर हिस्से

why_chain.step: Some plant parts need firm mechanical strength.
Thick lignified walls supply strong support.

unpack.example_or_place: Coconut husk fibres are a familiar example.
unpack.consequence: A dead mature cell can still provide useful structural support.
unpack.visual_verb: Thicken walls and resist bending.
unpack.level_extra: Learn both descendants and distinguish their shapes.

items.content: Aerenchyma: child of Parenchyma.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which parent contains aerenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is shown as a form of parenchyma within simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does aerenchyma differ from chlorenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Aerenchyma has conspicuous air spaces; chlorenchyma is distinguished by chloroplasts for photosynthesis.

teacher_understanding.question: Why are air spaces useful to aquatic plants?
teacher_understanding.answer: They provide internal paths for gases and can also aid buoyancy where plant parts are surrounded by water.

items.exam_note: Associate air spaces and aquatic adaptation, not chloroplasts alone.

terms.plain_meaning: बड़े हवा वाले खाली स्थानों वाला parenchyma
terms.everyday_image: स्पंज में जगह-जगह खाली जगहें

why_chain.step: Waterlogged or submerged parts need internal gas movement.
Large connected air spaces improve aeration and may aid floating.

unpack.example_or_place: Air-space tissue in many aquatic plants.
unpack.consequence: A structural modification of parenchyma suits a particular habitat.
unpack.visual_verb: Open air spaces between cells.
unpack.level_extra: The 'aer' association helps distinguish it from chlorenchyma.

items.content: Chlorenchyma: child of Parenchyma.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue group contains chlorenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: The tree places it beneath parenchyma, alongside aerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How does chlorenchyma differ from collenchyma?
teacher_understanding.answer: Chlorenchyma is chloroplast-containing parenchyma specialised for photosynthesis; collenchyma is mainly associated with flexible support.

teacher_understanding.question: How do chloroplasts enable its role?
teacher_understanding.answer: Their chlorophyll captures light energy used in photosynthesis to produce organic food.

items.exam_note: Distinguish chlorenchyma from collenchyma in spelling and function.

terms.plain_meaning: chloroplast वाला parenchyma, जो रोशनी की मदद से खाना बनाता है
terms.everyday_image: धूप में फैला हरा पत्ता

why_chain.step: Green plant parts need to use sunlight to make food.
Chloroplast-containing parenchyma performs photosynthesis.

unpack.example_or_place: Green tissue within leaves.
unpack.consequence: Parenchyma can specialise for food production as well as storage.
unpack.visual_verb: Illuminate chloroplast-containing cells.
unpack.level_extra: Chloro–green is a useful memory link, not a separate classification criterion.

items.content: Sclerenchyma fibers: child of Sclerenchyma.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which tissue contains these fibers?
teacher_understanding.answer: They are one of the two forms shown under sclerenchyma.

teacher_understanding.question: How do fibers differ from sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Fibers are typically elongated, narrow cells, while sclereids are often shorter and variable in shape.

teacher_understanding.question: How does an elongated form help support?
teacher_understanding.answer: Long, thick-walled cells can form bundles that resist pulling and strengthen plant parts.

items.exam_note: Know the parent group and the long-fibre form.

terms.plain_meaning: लंबे, पतले और मज़बूत दीवारों वाले सहारा देने के cells
terms.everyday_image: नारियल की भूसी के लंबे रेशे

why_chain.step: Plant parts need resistance to pulling forces.
Elongated thick-walled fibers strengthen them in bundles.

unpack.example_or_place: Fibres of coconut husk.
unpack.consequence: Shape helps distinguish two forms within the same tissue group.
unpack.visual_verb: Bundle long tapered cells.
unpack.level_extra: Retain the book spelling 'fibers'.

items.content: Sclereids: child of Sclerenchyma.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which larger group contains sclereids?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclereids belong to sclerenchyma, within simple permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How do sclereids compare with sclerenchyma fibers?
teacher_understanding.answer: Sclereids have varied shapes and are often relatively short; fibers are typically long and narrow. Both have thick, lignified walls.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can sclereids make a food feel gritty?
teacher_understanding.answer: Clusters of hard, thick-walled cells resist crushing, producing the gritty texture familiar in pear flesh.

items.exam_note: Pear grit is a useful application; sclereids remain simple tissue.

terms.plain_meaning: बहुत मोटी, कड़ी दीवार वाले अलग-अलग आकार के cells
terms.everyday_image: नाशपाती खाते समय महसूस होने वाले कड़क दाने

why_chain.step: Some regions need local hardness and protection.
Thick-walled sclereids provide that hardness.

unpack.example_or_place: Gritty cells in pear flesh.
unpack.consequence: Hard support need not take the form of long fibres.
unpack.visual_verb: Reveal hard cells within soft fruit.
unpack.level_extra: Do not define every sclereid as round; shapes vary.

items.content: Xylem: child of Complex permanent tissue.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which branch contains xylem?
teacher_understanding.answer: It belongs to complex permanent tissue, alongside phloem.

teacher_understanding.question: How does xylem's transport role differ from phloem's?
teacher_understanding.answer: Xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals, mainly from roots toward shoots; phloem transports organic food from sources to sinks.

teacher_understanding.question: How is long-distance water conduction possible?
teacher_understanding.answer: Connected water-conducting elements form pathways, with transpiration pull helping move water through the plant.

items.exam_note: Do not confuse water–mineral transport with food transport.

terms.plain_meaning: पानी और घुले minerals पहुँचाने वाला plant tissue
terms.everyday_image: जड़ों से पत्तों तक जाती पानी की लाइन

why_chain.step: Leaves need water and minerals absorbed by roots.
Xylem provides a conducting pathway across the plant.

unpack.example_or_place: Conducting tissue extending through roots, stem and leaves.
unpack.consequence: The classification links specialised cell combinations to transport.
unpack.visual_verb: Trace water upward through a stem.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the overgeneralisation that every xylem cell is dead.

items.content: Phloem: child of Complex permanent tissue.
items.type_note: The label identifies a subtype in the classification.

teacher_understanding.question: Which group contains phloem?
teacher_understanding.answer: The diagram places it with xylem under complex permanent tissue.

teacher_understanding.question: How does phloem differ from xylem in transported material?
teacher_understanding.answer: Phloem mainly transports organic food such as sucrose; xylem conducts water and dissolved minerals.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does food need to move away from a leaf?
teacher_understanding.answer: Roots, developing fruits and growing tissues may consume or store food without making enough of it themselves, so transport links food sources with these sinks.

prerequisites: Roots and growing organs need food
items.exam_note: Food movement is source-to-sink, not invariably downward.

terms.plain_meaning: बना हुआ खाना ज़रूरत या भंडारण वाले हिस्सों तक पहुँचाने वाला plant tissue
terms.everyday_image: रसोई से अलग-अलग कमरों तक खाना पहुँचाना

why_chain.step: Food-producing and food-using regions are often different.
Phloem distributes organic food between them.

unpack.example_or_place: Transport from mature leaves to growing roots or fruits.
unpack.consequence: Plants require separate coordinated pathways for different transport needs.
unpack.visual_verb: Send food from a leaf to growing organs.
unpack.level_extra: Avoid the trap that phloem transport is always downward.

items.where_on_page: bottom-left inset beside the classification leaves
items.content: A schematic upright shoot with leaves and green-highlighted growth regions. Apical meristem is labelled at the shoot tip; Intercalary meristem is labelled near a leaf or internode base below the tip; Lateral meristem is labelled along the side of the lower stem. Leader lines associate each label with a position, not a transport direction.
items.exam_note: Identify meristems from positions in an unlabelled schematic.

items.where_on_page: inset, leader line to top of shoot
items.content: Apical meristem: label points to the highlighted shoot tip.

teacher_understanding.question: What position does the apical label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies the growth region at the very top of the illustrated shoot.

teacher_understanding.question: Which feature distinguishes it from the other marked regions?
teacher_understanding.answer: It is the terminal tip rather than an intermediate band or a side region.

teacher_understanding.question: How does this position relate to growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Cell production near the tip, followed by enlargement, contributes to shoot elongation.

items.exam_note: Use the leader-line endpoint, not just the label's text position.

terms.plain_meaning: shoot की नोक पर नए cells बनाने वाला क्षेत्र
terms.everyday_image: ऊपर की ओर बढ़ती टहनी की नोक

why_chain.step: A shoot needs to extend at its growing end.
The inset marks apical meristem at that end.

unpack.example_or_place: The uppermost highlighted part of the pictured shoot.
unpack.consequence: The spatial picture anchors the apical branch of the tree.
unpack.visual_verb: Zoom to the tip and extend it.
unpack.level_extra: The inset shows a shoot; apical meristems also occur at root tips.

items.where_on_page: inset, left label beside upper stem band
items.content: Intercalary meristem: label points to a highlighted intermediate region near a leaf or internode base, below the shoot tip.

teacher_understanding.question: What position is marked intercalary?
teacher_understanding.answer: The label marks an intermediate growth region below the tip near a leaf or internode base.

teacher_understanding.question: Which other marked meristem is not at an intermediate band?
teacher_understanding.answer: The apical meristem is at the terminal shoot tip; the lateral label is placed along the side.

teacher_understanding.question: How does growth from such a region differ from tip growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: It adds cells in a region between mature parts, allowing local elongation without requiring the terminal tip itself to be the growth site.

items.exam_note: Recognise an intermediate growth region; do not generalise the schematic to every node.

terms.plain_meaning: सिरे के बजाय बीच के हिस्से में मौजूद बढ़ने का क्षेत्र
terms.everyday_image: घास के नीचे बचे हिस्से से नई बढ़त

why_chain.step: Some growth occurs between already differentiated parts.
The highlighted intermediate region visualises that position.

unpack.example_or_place: The green band below the tip in this inset.
unpack.consequence: Meristem position is not restricted to the outermost tip.
unpack.visual_verb: Highlight the band and lengthen above it.
unpack.level_extra: Link the schematic to grass leaf or internode bases without treating every node as meristematic.

items.where_on_page: inset, bottom label with line to lower stem side
items.content: Lateral meristem: label points to the side region of the lower stem.

teacher_understanding.question: What region does the lateral label identify?
teacher_understanding.answer: It identifies a region along the side of the stem rather than the terminal tip.

teacher_understanding.question: Which highlighted location corresponds to girth growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: The side-positioned lateral meristem is associated with increased thickness.

teacher_understanding.question: How does its spatial arrangement help explain girth growth?
teacher_understanding.answer: Divisions in lateral layers add tissue around the stem, increasing diameter rather than chiefly extending its tip.

items.exam_note: Side position links to thickness, not to a side branch growing in length.

terms.plain_meaning: तने की बगल में मोटाई बढ़ाने वाला क्षेत्र
terms.everyday_image: पतले पौधे का तना धीरे-धीरे मोटा होता है

why_chain.step: A stem may need to add thickness as the plant grows.
Cells added by lateral meristems increase girth.

unpack.example_or_place: The highlighted side strip in the lower stem of the inset.
unpack.consequence: The inset completes the position–growth distinction among three meristems.
unpack.visual_verb: Expand the stem outward.
unpack.level_extra: A lateral meristem is not simply any meristem on a lateral shoot.
